segments.text: We're back in the heart of the town.
Our final two stops really are just a few steps apart.
But let's take them one at a time.
Look to your left and find two towers which, at first glance, aren't even that easy to recognise as a pair.
There they are.
The Torri Gemelle, the Twin Towers.
The name suggests they're identical.
But, if you'll allow an architect's opinion, when looking at an old building you should use the word identical very carefully.
These towers date from the twelfth century.
So they're older than my Rocca, and by the early fourteenth century they formed part of Vicopisano's earlier Pisan fortification.
When Florence conquered the town, taking it from the Republic of Pisa in fourteen hundred and six, that old fortress was dismantled.
A few stops ago, I showed you the defensive system I designed to replace it.
The Twin Towers, though, remained standing.
And so, even today, we can read two different chapters of Vicopisano's history:
what remains of the Pisan fortification…
and the Florentine fortress built after the conquest.
Now look at the materials.
In the lower parts of the towers you'll find verrucano again, the stone we've seen several times along the way.
Higher up, the walls continue in brick.
This change tells us that both towers were altered and made taller over time, probably also to repair damage caused by the many sieges the town endured.
But the two towers didn't come through those events in the same way.
In the western one, the oldest stone section reaches about nineteen metres.
In the eastern tower, it reaches only eight.
Clearly, one of them needed far more rebuilding than the other.
Twins, then.
But with different scars.
The eastern tower also preserves the remains of Porta del Mercato, one of the old entrances to the fortified town.
Look closely and you can also make out a small doorway high above ground level.
It wasn't a door meant to be conveniently reached from the street.
Originally, access to the tower was through wooden structures that could be removed in times of danger.
But there's another reason why, seen from here, the two towers don't immediately look like a pair.
Now look at the building in front of you.
It's Vicopisano's Palazzo Comunale, the town hall.
Over time, it came to incorporate the Twin Towers and partly conceal their outlines, especially that of the western tower.
And since it's already in front of us…
I'd say it's time we gave it some attention too.
Just a few more steps.
Our final stop is right here.
